method: WebSearch + WebFetch (Brand New, Marketing Dive brand-strategy feed, Adweek, trade/press articles). Adweek '9 moves' paywalled beyond McDonald's item; several pages (UPI, phys.org, substack, jukebox) failed to fetch and were not used.

candidates.title: AI ads: the audience punishes pretending, not the tool (Fresh Step AI talking cats vs McDonald's NL pulled AI ad vs Coca-Cola AI ad that tested well)

sources.claim: Fresh Step (Clorox) made three 15s TV spots with AI agency RECE: AI-generated talking cats of different breeds/accents; brief to finished creative in 30 days at ~1/10 the cost of traditional production; live Nov 9; Clorox's Deb Crandall: 'We're not trying to fool anybody here.' Started from a business problem (odor-control perception dipping) and a consumer insight.
McDonald's Netherlands AI Christmas ad ('the most terrible time of the year') with slightly-off people and glitches was removed from YouTube three days after launch after backlash.
Coca-Cola 2025 'Holidays Are Coming' (Silverside AI, animals not human close-ups) scored 5.9 stars; few viewers mentioned AI; success credited to familiar assets (trucks, Santa, music).
AI holiday ads failed on authenticity: uncanny valley in near-human visuals breaks emotional connection; heavy AI read as cost-cutting over craft.

sources.publisher: Washington State University (Cicek, Gursoy, Lu; J. Hospitality Marketing & Management 2024)
sources.claim: Experiments with 1,000+ US adults, 8 categories: mentioning 'artificial intelligence' in product descriptions lowered emotional trust and purchase intention; stronger for high-risk products.

candidates.claim: Audiences don't reject AI per se; they reject near-real fakes that try to pass as real. Openly fictional AI (talking cats, animals) or AI carried by real brand codes fares better. (Synthesis = my interpretation, not a single study.)

gates.brand_fit: pass: designer/strategist voice, direct SMB utility (owners post AI images daily)
gates.story: strongest: tension 'tool vs pretending'; concrete image: talking cat vs balloon hands

lenses.red_team: Fresh Step results unknown (airs Nov 9): never claim it worked. Coke 2025 tested well despite online backlash: use as nuance, not as a failure. McDonald's NL is 2025: context, not news. WSU study is about product descriptions, not ads; say 'the word AI lowered trust' once with limits in caption. Thesis is an editorial synthesis: say 'my take'.
lenses.audience_psychology: Uncanny valley; perceived effort as a quality signal; deception aversion/persuasion knowledge: people forgive an obvious fiction, punish a disguised one.
lenses.brand_fit: Behnood is a designer: speaks with authority on craft; studio itself uses openly-labelled AI objects, so the message is coherent and honest.
